title: Explicit Meaning - Guided Practice
subject: rla
author: Chee Skool
reviewer: Chee Skool Explicit Meaning reference-skill review
reviewNotes: Phase 2 Explicit Meaning depth path. Teaches stated-vs-inferred distinctions, exact target matching, true-but-wrong details, qualifiers, accurate paraphrase, and explicit rule application. Existing multi-context Explicit Meaning Practice remains the independent follow-up. Excluded from random Mock until dedicated Mock-only material exists.

curriculum.learningObjective: Locate directly stated information, match the exact target of a question, preserve qualifiers and conditions, and reject reasonable ideas that the text does not actually state.

questions.prompt: Based on the equipment notice, decide whether each statement is directly stated or not stated.

items.text: A standard checkout must normally be returned before the employee's shift ends.
A contractor may take a checked-out tool home if a host employee approves it.
An overnight request must be submitted before 3 p.m.
Every covered tool requires an online training module before the first checkout.

explanation.answer: i1 and i3 are directly stated; i2 and i4 change what the notice says.
explanation.whyCorrect: The notice gives an end-of-shift deadline and a before-3-p.m. overnight request rule. Contractors are limited to on-site use, and only thermal cameras have the stated training requirement.
explanation.quickTip: Do not reward an answer for sounding reasonable. Ask whether the text actually says it.

questions.hint: Check each statement word by word. Watch for added permissions or words such as every.

questions.prompt: Which sentence directly states who is allowed to approve an overnight checkout request?

targets.text: Employees who need a tool overnight must submit a request before 3 p.m.
A team supervisor or shift lead may approve the request.
Once approved, the overnight checkout lasts until 10 a.m. on the next workday.
A host employee must check out the item for a contractor and remains responsible for its return.

explanation.answer: A team supervisor or shift lead may approve the request.
explanation.whyCorrect: That sentence answers the exact target: who may approve the request. The nearby sentences give the deadline, return time, or contractor responsibility instead.
explanation.quickTip: Turn the question into a target such as who, when, where, or why, then find the sentence that matches that target.

questions.hint: The question asks who. Ignore sentences that only tell you when to request or when to return the tool.

questions.prompt: According to the notice, when must a standard checkout normally be returned?

options.whyWrong: Before 3 p.m. is the deadline for submitting an overnight request, not for returning a standard checkout.

options.text: By 10 a.m. on the next workday
options.whyWrong: That deadline applies only after an overnight checkout has been approved.
Six weeks describes the pilot period, not a tool return deadline.

explanation.whyCorrect: The notice directly says standard checkouts must be returned before the employee's shift ends unless overnight use is approved.
explanation.quickTip: A number or time can be true in the passage and still answer the wrong question. Match the detail to the exact subject.

questions.prompt: Which phrase states the exception to the normal end-of-shift return deadline?

targets.text: unless an overnight checkout has been approved
until 10 a.m. on the next workday

explanation.answer: unless an overnight checkout has been approved
explanation.whyCorrect: The word unless introduces the condition that changes the normal end-of-shift rule. The other phrases give the normal deadline or times connected to the overnight process.
explanation.quickTip: Qualifier words such as unless, only, before, after, and at least can change the exact meaning of a rule.

questions.prompt: Which statement accurately paraphrases the training rule for thermal cameras?

options.text: Employees must repeat the 20-minute module every time they borrow a thermal camera.
options.whyWrong: The passage says the module does not need to be repeated after it has been completed.

options.text: Employees complete the 20-minute module before their first thermal-camera checkout, and later checkouts do not require repeating it.
Only contractors are required to complete the thermal-camera module.
options.whyWrong: The passage states the requirement for an employee borrowing a camera for the first time; it does not limit the rule to contractors.

options.text: The 20-minute module is required before an employee can check out any covered equipment.
options.whyWrong: The training requirement is stated specifically for thermal cameras, not for every covered tool.

explanation.whyCorrect: Choice B preserves both parts of the stated rule: training comes before the first thermal-camera checkout, and it does not need to be repeated later.
explanation.quickTip: A good paraphrase changes the wording without changing the limits or conditions.

questions.prompt: Rina's shift ends at 7 p.m. She submits a 2:45 p.m. overnight request for a torque wrench, and her shift lead approves it. According to the notice, when must she return the wrench?

options.whyWrong: That is the normal rule, but Rina has an approved overnight checkout.

options.text: By 10 a.m. on the next workday

options.whyWrong: Before 3 p.m. is the request deadline. It is not the return deadline.

options.text: Any time before the six-week pilot ends
options.whyWrong: The length of the pilot does not determine the return time for an individual checkout.

explanation.whyCorrect: Rina met the stated request deadline and received approval from an allowed approver, so the overnight rule applies: the checkout lasts until 10 a.m. on the next workday.
explanation.quickTip: For a rule with an exception, verify that the condition is met before applying the exception's deadline.
